title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
first_seen_basis: GitHub issue created_at; earliest evidenced repository observation
hf_date_evidence: No HF recommendation date asserted by this watch evidence package.

object.quote: We adopt the evolutionary model of Brennan and Lo (2011) , in which natural selection favors behaviors that maximize long-run population growth.

feedback.quote: agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search.

persistence.quote: individuals can also learn from their environment and pass their acquired improvements to later generations

study.quote: We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change.

verified_scope_policy: feed/taxonomy.yaml and feed/prompts/harness_gate.md: subsequent tasks OR improvement rounds, with actual external artifact modification
reason_zh: 理论比较达尔文、拉马克及 Agent 主导演化的适应速度、搜索成本与评价目标错设。DGM/AIDE² 只是动机及相关工作；形式化对象是一般继承行为和候选模型/Agent，而非专门研究外部 Harness 工件的反馈演化。归一般 RSI 理论/安全，排除出 Harness 专题。
persistence_boundary: Theoretical inheritance across generations is modeled; a specific reusable external Harness artifact is not identified.
limitations: Citing self-modifying agents as motivation does not establish Harness-specific theory.
Theorems and simulations were not independently reproved or rerun.
summary_zh: 本文用一般演化模型比较自然选择、可继承学习和 Agent 自主搜索的适应速度及成本，并分析评价目标错设时更强搜索为何可能更快偏离真实目标。研究并不专门限定外部 Harness 工件，归一般 RSI 理论与安全讨论。
summary_en: This theoretical study compares natural selection, inherited learning, and agent-directed search, including their adaptation rates, costs, and behavior under a misspecified evaluator. It models general inherited behavior rather than specifically the feedback-driven evolution of external harness artifacts.
